data.scenario_text: A <m>30</m>-foot monument casts a shadow <m>30</m> feet long on level ground.
data.find_task: Find the angle of elevation of the sun. Do not round until the final answer; then round to two decimal places as necessary.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the right angle marked and only the two given lengths written in: the leg opposite \theta is 30\text{ ft} and the leg adjacent to \theta is 30\text{ ft}. The third side is not given, so it stays unlabeled, and the angle should not be filled in.

Part (b). Both given quantities are lengths and the unknown is an angle, so the answer comes from an inverse function. In the triangle the given sides are the leg opposite \theta and the leg adjacent to \theta; the ratio built from exactly those two sides is tangent, \tan\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}, so we solve \tan\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} for \theta using the inverse tangent.

Substituting and computing, \theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{30}{30}\right).

This gives \theta \approx 45.00^\circ, so the angle of elevation of the sun is \boxed{45.00^\circ}.
